intro.title: Build typed shared UI package API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed API for a shared UI package, which is a collection of reusable components like buttons and inputs. You'll learn how to use TypeScript interfaces to define strict contracts for the props each component accepts, ensuring type safety. The main technologies involved are TypeScript interfaces and generic types to create flexible, reusable component definitions. By the end, you'll have a foundational package structure that can be shared across projects with full type checking and autocompletion.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential when building component libraries like Material-UI, Ant Design, or internal design systems at companies like Airbnb or Shopify. Developers use typed shared UI packages to create consistent, reusable components such as buttons, modals, and data tables across multiple applications. For example, a dashboard application might import a typed Chart component that enforces proper data structure validation, while an e-commerce platform ensures all product cards have consistent props. This approach prevents bugs during integration and provides excellent developer experience through autocomplete and type checking in IDEs.
